items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I can remember when, you know Jimmy Forrest was a great player. He was on that same band.

ctx.x: Well there’s a lot of places where I thought the people would never ever wake up. A lot of places he never made no impression at all. It was a horrible thing to say, but a lot of places he never made no impression at all. And some places he made an impression you know, made good impressions. They always loved Bird at the Savoy Ballroom. They loved Bird all over New York City. New York loved him. But it took him so long to decide, well what are we going to do about him, or what are we going to do with him. I…
Now you worked with some great Texas Tenors yourself, Buddy Tate? Some great recordings.

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: But Jimmy Forrest come back around and when Bird get through blowing, they never even clapped their hands. But when Forrest get through, the house would break up.

ctx.x: Because they understood while -- how would you say it? I don't mean they understood it musically for the -- you know what I mean. But they understood that they like it. They liked it. See, when we went to New York, we'd be in New York, just blowing. Bird would get up and blow "Body and Soul" -- we had a heck of an arrangement on "Body and Soul" -- and he'd blow that "Body and Soul" and ain't nothing else to blow. But Jimmy Forrest come back around and when Bird get through blowing, they never even clapped their…
You mean they didn't hear it.
